PullRequest.Title: sessions: polish scheduled-message previews and inline editing
PullRequest.Body:
Adds a preview to the scheduled-message clock in the sessions list, with each message, the time remaining, and Edit, Send Now, and Cancel Schedule actions.

Scheduled messages keep their inline editor, now with Cancel and a timed Send split button such as "Send Today at 3:07 PM". The primary button saves for that time; the dropdown changes the time. Hover or focus the relative timestamp to see the exact local date and time, without seconds or a time-zone suffix.

This builds on #348610 and preserves its New Session composer, Send Now, model configuration, and scheduling fixes. Editing stays inside the scheduled prompt and never replaces the main composer's draft.

### Try it

1. Enable `chat.automations.enabled` and `sessions.sendLater.enabled`, then schedule a message in an existing chat.
2. Hover over or click that session's clock. The clock stays in place when the row's actions appear.
3. Choose Edit to return to the original message. Use the timed Send button to save, its dropdown to reschedule, or Cancel to leave the schedule unchanged.
4. Hover or keyboard-focus a scheduled message's timestamp to see its exact local send time.

The preview also opens with Enter or Space when the clock is focused. Tab reaches the message actions, arrow keys move between them, and Escape closes the preview.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The cache's only disposal/replacement sites, row-template pooling, interval ownership, and request-to-automation closure chain are directly traceable. Retention does not depend on timing or a failed operation. Exact retained bytes depend on attachments and how many row templates were hovered.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Detached preview DOM, ActionBars, per-message timers/listeners, and original automation/request snapshots including embedded attachment strings.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One stale card per previously hovered row template, bounded by the virtual list's peak template pool, not by all sessions ever visited. Each card retains all of that session's previewed requests and their attachment bytes; several image-bearing cards can therefore retain substantial memory.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary long-lived renderer memory and continuing timer work after preview content is no longer needed.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The clock used a static text hover and retained no scheduled-request card, ActionBars, request snapshots, or per-message update timers.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Preview stores are now owned by the reusable row template, rather than the displayed hover. Closing the preview, cancelling its last request, and recycling the row do not release the cached card; only constructing a different card in that template or disposing the entire template does.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line registers card-store disposal only with template.disposables, and lines 1968-1970 cache the rendered card. The new empty-request branch at 1956-1957 returns without clearing that cache. Existing disposeElement only clears elementDisposables, while RowCache retains released templates until list disposal.
Findings.Title: Release cached preview resources after the hover closes
Findings.Impact: Hovering scheduled messages with screenshots or embedded selections and then cancelling them can leave their original attachment snapshots retained for the lifetime of the sessions list, even after their schedules have been deleted. Repeating this across row templates retains additional large snapshots and leaves hidden preview timers running.
Findings.Evidence: renderScheduledRequestsCard installs one minute interval and document visibility listener per timed message through renderScheduledRequestTime. Its action wrappers at sessionScheduledRequestsCard.ts:67 capture request and action; ScheduledChatsService.items creates those actions with closures over the original automation. Those descriptors can contain base64 image/file contents (scheduledChatRequest.ts:45-69). Consequently a cancelled/deleted request's original attachment data, ActionBars, detached DOM and timers remain reachable from the cached card after the hover is hidden.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep a card alive across refreshes while its hover is open, but dispose its store and remove the cached entry when the preview is closed and no longer needed. Also invalidate stale entries on row-resource replacement or request removal; avoid retaining full request/action objects when only their IDs are needed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, refresh, filter, and scroll the sessions list with scheduled-message indicators.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible row rendering installs indicator listeners and observes the scheduled-resource set. Preview construction and the new scheduled-request grouping are deferred until the request map is read by a hover/action; they do not eagerly restore chats or issue automation commands during list rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible/recycled row templates and total outstanding scheduled requests. Grouping copies growing arrays within each session, but normal small groups do not establish an actionable performance regression; rows remain virtualized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI rendering plus existing observable updates. There is no per-session asynchronous boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Indicators are reused for the same resource. The new derived grouping reads already-available service items, not a separate provider catalogue. No new filesystem/network lookup or negative-cache retry is introduced by list refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that row rendering does not construct preview cards or load chat models eagerly, based on the deferred hover-options callback and HoverService setupDelayedHover implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of outstanding requests per session is not established; very large groups would make array copying more noticeable, but there is no realistic high-cardinality trigger established for a separate finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate startup, scrolling, eager-load, or boundary-fan-out finding. Preview-cache lifecycle is addressed separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open scheduled-message previews by mouse or keyboard, close them, cancel messages, and recycle their rows.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hover-options resolution reads the grouped request map, serializes the cache key, and constructs the card synchronously on a cache miss. Closing the hover does not dispose the card store, so its retained resources and minute updates continue off the interaction's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify the session's request IDs, full text, timing, description, and action metadata for cache identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialization of that session's requests on each hover-options resolution, including warm card-cache hits; no serialization of all sessions' prompt text in this helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The indicator provided a constant text hover without serializing scheduled requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before preview display. No independently material serialization latency was established for typical requests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cached card per hovered row template, bounded by the virtual list's peak template pool. Each card can contain multiple requests, each with a timer and action closures reaching the original automation and embedded attachment bytes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Card creation is synchronous, not concurrent provider work. Each cached timed message independently registers a 60-second interval and document visibility listener. Updates skip formatting while the document is hidden but continue for detached cards while the window is visible.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cards are keyed by serialized request presentation. Replacement happens only when another nonempty request set resolves a different key in the same template. Empty requests, hover closure, and row recycling do not invalidate the cache; disposal is tied to template destruction. WeakMap ownership does not release live pooled templates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the only cache replacement/disposal sites, disposeElement versus disposeTemplate, RowCache pooling, timer ownership, card action closures, service action closures, and embedded attachment capture.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Peak template count and attachment sizes vary. Capture explicitly supports embedded base64 screenshots and file selections, making substantial retained snapshots realistic; this is bounded by the template pool, not unbounded session history.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity cache-lifecycle regression: closed/stale previews retain detached UI, timers, and original request/attachment snapshots.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose Edit in a preview or an existing scheduled message to open its inline editor without replacing the composer draft.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: startEditing publishes the edit state, checks registered visible widgets, and navigates to the original chat only when it is not already visible. Navigation resolves the session, activates its view, and may restore that single chat's model/history.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the explicitly selected session through provider resolvers and open/reveal its original chat. Local Agent Host resolution has a cached surfaced-resource path; legacy migration may probe the host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One navigation for the selected request, only when no matching registered widget is visible. Provider resolvers are tried serially until one resolves; there is no operation per other scheduled request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: startEditing only published state and did not reveal an offscreen chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Navigation/session readiness can delay availability of an offscreen inline editor; this is required to reveal the selected chat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For a cold selected chat, obtain provider-backed chat content through getOrCreateChatSession and restore its history; provider transport may cross the host boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one underlying in-flight model load per selected chat resource after coalescing. Already loaded models are acquired without another provider load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editing an offscreen scheduled message did not initiate chat navigation/loading from startEditing; users had to open that chat separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold model/history restoration is needed to display the requested original inline editor, not performed during preview rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered chat-widget count for the visible-widget check, provider resolver count, and the selected chat's history size. Other scheduled messages do not multiply model loads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One selected edit/navigation; existing navigation cancellation and resource-keyed model-load coalescing remain in effect. No Promise.all over scheduled messages is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Matching visible widgets bypass navigation. ChatService reuses existing models, coalesces remote loads by resource, and serializes replacement after abandoned loads. startEditing returns early for the same active edit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in conditional reachability and coalescing from the service, navigation, ChatView, and ChatService implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold chat history size and provider latency vary. The new load is intentional first-use work needed to reveal the requested editor, not redundant background fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable regression: conditional navigation is necessary feature work, and visible chats avoid reopening.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display scheduled requests and edit controls with relative and absolute local timestamps.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rendered scheduled rows format their labels and add a second time element. Nonediting rows now own an additional absolute-label timer; editing rows replace relative formatting with absolute formatting. DOM writes occur only when a label changes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendered scheduled rows, plus separately cached preview messages. Accessible text also formats the selected scheduled request. No transcript-wide or per-frame loop is added by the timestamp change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent minute timers on the UI event loop, with document-hidden checks; no subprocess, provider call, synchronous geometry read, or nested layout is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: safeIntl.DateTimeFormat returns Lazy objects, so formatter construction is deferred and shared. Previous-label checks suppress unchanged DOM writes. scheduledRequestDisposables is cleared on rerender and disposal, preventing timer accumulation in transcript rows.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected safeIntl laziness, the label renderer, renderer disposal paths, and changed CSS. Timestamp transitions use opacity/transform rather than a new synchronous measurement path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The count of simultaneously rendered scheduled rows varies, but the additional minute-frequency formatting is small and properly scoped. No concrete jank mechanism was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate rendering or timer-lifecycle finding for transcript rows; stale preview timers are covered by the reported cache issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Save/reschedule an inline edit or invoke Send Now and Cancel Schedule from the preview.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected action is resolved against current service items. Save may capture newly changed attachments, then awaits one authoritative update; Send Now dispatches one automation and observes acceptance; cancellation preserves recovery, disables the selected schedule, restores its original input, and deletes that definition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the selected definition update/run, or cancellation's disable followed by deletion, through the owning automation store and wait for authoritative catalogue state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One update per save/reschedule, one run request per Send Now unless an active run is reused, and the existing sequential disable/delete operations for one cancelled definition. No command is sent for every previewed row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing scheduled-message actions used the same service/store paths with the same per-selected-request boundary counts; this PR adds a preview entry point and changes button presentation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User action completion awaits its authoritative operation; the card is hidden first. Ongoing run completion remains separately observed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture newly introduced/changed attachment content through model references or file reads before saving; retained original attachments are reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only applicable input attachments not reusable from the existing handoff are captured. A per-input Promise.all already existed; image reads occur only when bytes are not already supplied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same saveEditedRequest/captureRequest implementation and attachment reuse rules already performed this work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required capture completes before the authoritative save, unchanged by the button/preview changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or load the original chat model to restore cancelled input, and persist the existing handoff/recovery transitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected chat-model acquire per conversation cancellation, with the shared ChatService warm-model and in-flight-load reuse behavior; fixed recovery writes for that action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing Cancel Schedule action performed the same recovery, model acquisition, and deletion sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cancellation recovery waits for the selected model and authoritative deletion, as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected automation, that request's changed attachments, and its original chat history on a cold cancellation path; not the number of sessions or all preview rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Save controls and service state guard duplicate saves. Cancellation's dependent operations remain sequential. Existing attachment capture concurrency and host dispatch behavior are not increased by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Actions are re-resolved by request/action ID, preventing cached preview callbacks from requiring provider reads. Store conflict checks use projected in-memory catalogue state. Existing model reuse and attachment reuse are preserved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced preview callbacks through ScheduledChatsService and the Agent Host store, including update guards, run reuse, dispatch, recovery, and attachment capture.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency and attachment sizes affect action duration, but there is no added action fan-out or new capture frequency in these paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance regression in action execution. Retention of the old card after these actions is the separately reported issue.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 15 changed files and all diff pages. Reported one introduced cache-lifecycle memory regression in scheduled-preview ownership, with cardinality bounded by pooled row templates. Investigated and rejected separate speculative issues around grouping, full-text cache keys, timestamp formatting, navigation, and automation fan-out. No evidence warranted recording a shipped performance-regression fix.
